structured_output.assessment:
The revisions are sound overall. The abstract is unchanged and keeps the author's style. The self-similar versus participant-selected neutral voice comparison stays central, and gaze contingency and Jev remain shared apparatus. The design facts are intact: one practice trial in the first counterbalanced voice, two 40-trial blocks, final retrospective questionnaires only, and no participant outcomes. Engineering evidence stays separate. Questionnaire items, spoken instructions, identifiers, math and thresholds are unchanged. No citations were deleted or attributed to the wrong source.

The hated introduction sentence has been replaced with connected scholarly prose, and similar phrasing in Chapters 5, 8 and 9 was also fixed. Seven issues remain:
- In Chapter 2's synthesis, "compares it" points back to "speech" instead of the self-similar voice.
- The Method rationale now assumes participants "rely on" the voice, but reliance is an exploratory outcome.
- The Sabouni paragraph restates the control comparison twice.
- The discussion's gaze-coupling sentence repeats the sentence before it.
- The opening-cue-to-selection interval is described as if it measured clip duration.
- The System chapter opening narrows the comparison to "voice experiences", leaving out performance.
- The Appendix D figure-provenance register doesn't mention the new figure reconstructed from development Run 26, and it describes every figure as a schematic or interface illustration.

issues.old: The present design gives speech an ongoing instructional role and compares it with a neutral voice that already reflects the participant's preference.
issues.new: The present design gives speech an ongoing instructional role and compares the self-similar voice with a neutral voice that already reflects the participant's preference.
issues.reason: "It" grammatically refers to "speech", so the sentence compares speech with a neutral voice instead of naming the central comparison: the self-similar voice versus the neutral voice.

issues.old: relative to the control. Relative to the control condition, the audio cue therefore changed one aspect of search behavior without a detectable reduction in completion time. This supports examining
issues.new: relative to the control. The study therefore supports examining
issues.reason: Leftover redundancy: the middle sentence repeats the previous one almost word for word and stacks a second "relative to the control". Removing it keeps the reported finding and the conclusion about attention allocation.

issues.old: they create repeated occasions on which participants rely on the assigned voice;
issues.new: they create repeated occasions on which participants receive guidance in the assigned voice;
issues.reason: Overstates certainty. Reliance is measured as an exploratory outcome (RQ3, custom reliance and guidance-use items), so the design rationale should not assume it. This restores the original meaning: repeated opportunities to receive guidance.

issues.old: The system will also retain the interval from opening-cue onset to selection, preserving the opening instruction and subsequent search within a broader timing measure. This record permits examination of differences in opening-clip duration across voices, while active completion time remains the primary outcome.
issues.new: The system will also retain the broader interval from opening-cue onset to selection, which includes the time spent receiving the opening instruction. Because prepared opening clips can differ in duration across voices, this record remains informative, although active completion time is the primary outcome.
issues.reason: The revision implies that this interval measures clip-duration differences, but it does not. The original reason was that clip duration differs across voices, which is why the broader interval is kept. The phrase "preserving the opening instruction ... within a broader timing measure" is also awkward.

issues.old: This coupling complicates interpretation, because reduced gaze availability can both reduce measurement coverage and suspend guidance.
issues.new: This coupling complicates interpretation, because a gap in gaze availability is not simply missing data when it also suspends guidance.
issues.reason: Leftover redundancy: the previous sentence already says poor tracking reduces measurement coverage. This sentence repeats that ("reduced ... reduce") instead of making the original point, which was that a gaze gap is more than missing data.

issues.old: Together, these functions support the comparison of voice experiences, with the decision provider held common across conditions.
issues.new: Together, these functions support the voice comparison, with the decision provider held common across conditions.
issues.reason: "Voice experiences" narrows the platform's purpose to experience only, but active completion time is the primary outcome.

issues.old: An actual Trial Review capture shows its explicitly synthetic bundled demonstration. Figure sources and provenance are listed in \path{figures/README.md}. These figures are explanatory schematics or interface illustrations, not measured participant results.
issues.new: An actual Trial Review capture shows its explicitly synthetic bundled demonstration, and a three-panel reconstruction shows the recorded scene from headset development Run 26. Figure sources and provenance are listed in \path{figures/README.md}. These figures are explanatory schematics, interface illustrations, or reconstructions of development recordings, not measured participant results.
issues.reason: The provenance register leaves out the new figure reconstructed from real recorded development data (Run 26). It also calls every figure a schematic or interface illustration, which contradicts the Chapter 3 caption saying the recording supplies the object geometry, positions and poses.
